Attach Sample-Level Metadata to a List of Seurat Objects

Source: R/includeMetadata.R
includeMetadata.Rd

Joins a sample-level table – treatment group, genotype, timepoint, and so on – onto a named list of Seurat objects, typically the output of seuratFrom10x(). Each row of metadata describes one sample; every other column becomes a metadata column on that sample's object, broadcast across all of its cells.

Usage

includeMetadata(objList, metadata, overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

objList

Named list of Seurat objects, one per sample, as returned by seuratFrom10x().

metadata

Data frame with one row per sample. Sample names come from a Sample column if present, otherwise from the rownames, and must match names(objList). Every remaining column is attached.

overwrite

Logical. Whether to replace metadata columns that already exist on the objects. Defaults to FALSE, which errors instead. Ident is reserved and cannot be set either way – it identifies the sample of origin and is what mergeSeurat() verifies after merging.

Value

objList with the new columns attached, in the same order and with the same names. Column types are preserved, including factor levels – though note that Seurat::merge() flattens factors to character, so a factor column survives on the list but not through mergeSeurat().

Details

This is deliberately separate from the manifest seuratFrom10x() accepts. That manifest is a run-level table – one row per Cell Ranger outs/ directory – and a multiplexed run expands into many samples, so a single manifest row cannot carry per-sample assignments. metadata is a sample-level table instead, keyed on the names of objList. That works identically for multiplexed and non-multiplexed input, because by the time the list exists the distinction is already gone.

Samples are identified by a Sample column if metadata has one, and by its rownames otherwise. A Sample column takes precedence, and is used as the key rather than attached as metadata.

Every column must be populated for every object in objList: a sample with no row in metadata, or an NA or blank value in any column, is an error. This is what keeps the result safe to mergeSeurat(). merge() will happily combine an object carrying a Treatment column with one that lacks it, silently filling the gap with NA for every cell of the un-annotated sample; requiring completeness up front makes that state unreachable.

Rows matching no object are ignored with a warning, so one master sheet can cover a whole experiment while you work on a subset of it. A mistyped sample name is still caught, since it also leaves some object without a row.

See also

seuratFrom10x(), which produces the named list this expects, and mergeSeurat(), which consumes the annotated result.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
seurat_list <- seuratFrom10x(
  path        = "/path/to/Pool1/outs",
  multi = TRUE
)

# one row per demuxed sample, however many the run produced
sheet <- data.frame(
  Sample    = c("Sample_A", "Sample_B"),
  Treatment = c("Control", "Bleomycin"),
  Timepoint = c("D0", "D21")
)

annotated <- includeMetadata(seurat_list, sheet)
merged    <- mergeSeurat(annotated)

table(merged$Ident, merged$Treatment)
} # }
